extracted.intended_audience: citizen commenters, advocacy groups, and researchers interested in effective participation in federal agency rulemaking (notice-and-comment)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing effective notice-and-comment submissions to federal agencies, based on empirical findings about who participates and which comments influence rulemaking. Emphasizes presence, agency-specific tailoring, iterative/coalition credibility, and providing substantive information absent from industry filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show up at all / citizen participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizen commenters are extremely rare; a substantive comment from a non-business commenter has outsized marginal value simply because the docket is so unbalanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a single well-formed citizen or community comment can stand out. Prioritize submitting something substantive rather than abstaining; presence itself is a key component of influence when non-business voices are absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match the agency's decisional context
rubrics_metrics.description: Different agencies respond to different coalitions and analytical conventions (e.g., EPA dominated by environmental and industry coalitions; NHTSA industry-heavy; HUD more diverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor comments to the specific agency's analytical language, evidentiary expectations, and decision-making style. What counts as adequate engagement and persuasive evidence varies by agency—align framing, metrics, and references accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue-network, iterative engagement and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are most influential within issue networks where commenters have established credibility through repeated participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build on prior submissions, position papers, and research from the commenter or allied organizations. Show continuity with past filings, cite earlier contributions, and demonstrate ongoing engagement to increase persuasive weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of voices matters (bias is in who shows up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies listen to commenters broadly; there is no uniform filtering bias in whose voices get heard given who comments. The practical bias is that some groups simply don't participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substantive comment from an under-represented group is genuinely heard—therefore increasing participation from absent perspectives changes the docket's informational balance and can affect agency cognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent an under-represented perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment represent a perspective absent or under-represented in the docket?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight unique viewpoints (e.g., community impacts, marginalized stakeholder concerns) that industry actors are unlikely to supply. Emphasize lived experience, public-interest framing, or constituency-specific harms to fill informational gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build on established expertise and prior engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment build on the commenter's (or allied organizations') established expertise and prior engagement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the author's or organization's credentials, prior submissions, research, or participation in the issue network. Use references to earlier filings and demonstrate continuity to bolster credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor comment to the agency's analytical conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the comment tailored to the specific agency's analytical conventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the agency's preferred analytical frameworks, statutory standards, and technical terminology. Address the specific regulatory questions posed in the notice and format arguments in the way the agency typically evaluates evidence and cost/benefit tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide substantive content industry will not supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment provide substantive content (data, analysis, narrative) that a regulated industry would not supply?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include original data, independent analysis, qualitative narratives, or community impact evidence that corrects or complements industry-submitted materials. Offer alternative factual bases or harms that industry filings tend to omit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify as part of an issue-network position
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment identify itself as part of an issue-network position (citing aligned research, prior comments, or coalitions)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite allied research, reference coalition statements or previous coordinated comments, and situate the submission within a broader network position. This signals alignment, builds credibility, and shows the agency that the comment is part of sustained engagement rather than an isolated statement.
